_comment: Version-controlled patches re-applied to plugin CACHES at startup. A plugin cache is managed like node_modules (clobbered on every plugin update), so a useful local edit can't just be synced as a file — it must be (a) tracked here and (b) re-applied per host. The applier (apply-plugin-patches.py) is idempotent + FAIL-LOUD: it never force-applies, and emits a WARN (without failing startup) if a plugin update made a patch stale. A stale patch is a signal to re-base it — or better, upstream the change so the patch retires. See README.md.

patches.desc: discord:access — route all 8 mutating subcommands through the locked `scripts/access-mutate.py` CLI (access_store.mutate_access_file) instead of freehand Read/Write, and add the safer `group append` / `group rm-allow` subcommands (append-without-replace; avoids the lock-yourself-out trap of stock `group add`, which overwrites the channel allowlist). Upstream candidate for claude-plugins-official. NOTE: the marker was previously the literal string "group append", which collides with this same string occurring naturally in the pristine plugin's own freehand heading — apply_one() checked the marker before ever attempting the dry-run, so it silently reported "already applied" and the patch was never actually applied in production. Keep this marker specific to the patched (CLI-routed) content, never a phrase that could occur in unrelated prose.
